body.p: File conflicts happen when two branches modify the same part of a file in incompatible ways and Git cannot merge them automatically. Conflicts can occur during a merge, rebase, cherry-pick, or revert.
In Git Staging, conflicted files appear in Unstaged files. To resolve a conflict, follow these steps:

ol.li:
Open a conflicted file in the compare editor to view the differences between its local and incoming versions. To open a file in the compare editor, on Unstaged files, double-click it. Alternatively, right-click it and select Open in Compare Editor.
Conflicted file context menu

Choose how to resolve the conflict:
To keep changes from both versions, use the compare editor to choose which changes to keep. Select Apply when done.
To accept one version entirely, right-click the conflicted file, select , and choose Resolve Using Mine to keep the local version, or Resolve Using Theirs to accept the incoming version.
To mark a file as resolved without editing it, right-click it and select Mark as Resolved.

body.p: Resolved files are staged automatically and appear in Staged files.

During an in-progress operation, Git Staging identifies the current operation and lists conflicted files in Unstaged files. The Git History view shows the relationship between the source and destination commits. For details, see .
